1.explanation: Both bash.js and shell.js define the grammar rules for Bash and shell-compatible highlighting. bash.js is missing patterns for meta-operators (|, >, <), line-continuations (\\$), here-documents (<<), here-strings (<<<), and subshell segments ($(…)). shell.js is an alias that reuses or slightly adapts bash.js. To restore proper highlighting of those constructs, the regex modes in these two files need to be updated or extended to include tokens matching pipes, redirections, heredocs, here-strings, and subshell syntax.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting Bash code, common shell metacharacters and constructs—such as pipes (|), line-continuation backslashes (\), I/O redirections (> and <), here-docs (<<) and here-strings (<<<), and subshell expansions ($(…))—are not being recognized or styled by highlight.js’s bash (and its alias shell) language definitions. In the provided screenshots you can see the same snippet highlighted in “shell” mode (which works) vs. “bash” mode (which doesn’t highlight those elements at all).

2.explanation:
The two language definition files for the shell family control how these tokens are recognized and styled.  

• src/languages/bash.js is the primary highlighter for bash syntax. It needs new or improved regex patterns and mode definitions for pipes, redirections, heredocs, backslash-continuation, and subshell expansions.  
• src/languages/shell.js is the alias/extension for generic shell (sh) syntax. It sources or inherits from bash.js, so it also must be updated for consistency.  

No other language definitions or core engine files are involved: all missing tokens are shell-specific, so editing these two files is necessary to add or tweak the matching rules for the missing operators and constructs.
2.bug_scenario:
In both the shell and bash code blocks the common shell operators and constructs are not being highlighted. Specifically:
- The pipe character (|) is treated as plain text
- The line-continuation backslash (\) at end-of-line is not highlighted
- Stream redirection tokens (<, >) are not picked up
- The heredoc and here-string markers (<<, <<<) are ignored
- Subshell invocations ($(…)) aren’t recognized as a unit or given any special styling

The screenshots show identical sequences of commands for “shell” and “bash” modes, but none of these operators are colored or tokenized, so these elements are all rendered as default text.
